WHERE THINGS STAND

AddvancedFocus: what’s here today.

Working demo

Built and working

  • An interactive AddvancedFocus concept with three everyday situations and two energy levels
  • Two- and five-minute sessions you can pause with a return note, stop without marking the step complete, or undo a completion
  • This website and its accessibility statement
Try the working demo
In development

What we’re building

  • AI-assisted task initiation and planning
  • Flexible routines and household coordination
  • Privacy, affordability, and user control

Not yet decided

  • Public launch date
  • Pricing
  • Supported platforms
  • AI provider
  • Data practices

We’ll explain these before public release.

How we’re building it

  1. Current concept

    Make the interaction tangible

    Explore smaller starting points, flexible focus sessions, and a way back after interruptions through the interactive website prototype.

  2. Planned development

    Add useful intelligence

    Develop AI-assisted ways to turn everyday intentions into manageable actions, while keeping suggestions understandable and editable.

  3. Before public release

    Clarify the full experience

    Evaluate accessibility and reliability, define personal-data controls, and communicate supported platforms, pricing, and product limitations.

This is a statement of direction. Scope and sequencing may change as development progresses.

THE FUTURE PRODUCT FAMILY

Different needs.
One shared commitment.

Each concept addresses a distinct everyday challenge and has its own page with the intended workflow, planned capabilities, and questions.

CareBridgeStoryReadyClearCuePlainPathStepAbleSayAbleSensoryScoutOpenCall
  • Family care coordination

    CareBridge

    Less paperwork. More progress.An AI family assistant being designed to help parents coordinate evaluations, therapies, school services, and the follow-ups that connect them.    Concept→
  • Visual stories & transitions

    StoryReady

    Make the unfamiliar feel familiar.Personalized visual preparation for children who benefit from predictable routines, clear sequences, and support with unfamiliar experiences.    Concept→
  • Speech comprehension & follow-through

    ClearCue

    Hear it. Understand it. Remember it.An auditory processing assistant focused on understanding and remembering spoken information, including for people with ADHD, auditory processing differences, or hearing difficulties.    Concept→
  • Written information & action

    PlainPath

    Make complicated things understandable.A cognitive accessibility assistant that would help people understand complex documents and follow through on what those documents ask them to do.    Concept→
  • Independent living skills

    StepAble

    Independence, one step at a time.An independent-living coach being conceived for people with intellectual or developmental disabilities, autism, and other cognitive support needs.    Concept→
  • Communication & expression

    SayAble

    Your voice. Your choices.An AI-assisted communication concept for people who have difficulty speaking, with an emphasis on personal expression and control over every message.    Concept→
  • Sensory access & outings

    SensoryScout

    Explore the world on your terms.A sensory accessibility assistant intended to help people plan outings around their preferences for noise, lighting, crowds, and predictability.    Concept→
  • Accessible scam awareness

    OpenCall

    A clearer pause before you act.An accessibility-focused direction for OpenCall: help people with cognitive support needs recognize potentially fraudulent messages and calls, understand the warning signs, and consider safer next steps.    Concept→

A CONNECTED VISION

Useful on its own.
Connected by choice.

The long-term goal is shared support without requiring the entire suite.

We envision optional sharing of accessibility preferences, authorized reminders, and relevant context across Biro.dev products. Each connection should be understandable, permission-based, and controlled by the person using it.

Affordability, privacy, accessibility by design, and offline functionality where practical are intended foundations of the product family. Core accessibility should be part of the experience, rather than a premium upgrade.

UNDERSTANDING THE PORTFOLIO

A shared mission.
Clear expectations.

How are you deciding what to build first?

AddvancedFocus remains the flagship. Future products would be evaluated around the everyday need, technical feasibility, accessibility, privacy, and the input required from the people who would use them. This portfolio is a direction, not a commitment to simultaneous launches.

Can I help shape a product?

Yes. Each product page includes a direct email link for sharing a perspective or question with Jonathan. You can describe the situation, the support that would help, and anything an app should avoid adding to your workload. There is no requirement to share a diagnosis or sensitive personal information.
